interviewBank.q: Why does ::before need a content property?
interviewBank.answer: Generated boxes only exist when content is set, even an empty string. Without it the pseudo-element has no box to style.
It is read by some screen readers depending on the content and browser, and it is not reliably selectable or translatable. Real content belongs in the markup.

defenseBank.q: A learner puts the entire button label in ::before.
defenseBank.answer: If the generated content fails, the control has no label, and it may not be exposed correctly. The label belongs in the markup; pseudo-elements are decoration.
steps: Move the label into the element.

defenseBank.q: Why prefer a real element over an overlay pseudo-element?
defenseBank.answer: A pseudo-element cannot receive events or be individually selected or announced, so anything interactive needs a real element.

Which property is required for ::after to render?

title: CSS Transitions and Transformations
goal: Animate state changes smoothly and move, rotate, scale or skew elements without affecting layout.

topics.title: Transitions need four decisions
topics.body: Transition property, duration, timing function aur delay batata hai. Sirf un properties par lagta hai jinke beech browser interpolate kar sakta hai.
topics.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <title>Transition</title>
  <style>
    .btn { background: #2563eb; color: #fff; padding: 10px 16px; border: 0; border-radius: 8px; transition: background-color 180ms ease, transform 180ms ease; }
    .btn:hover { background: #1d4ed8; transform: translateY(-2px); }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <button class="btn" type="button">Hover me</button>
</body>
</html>
topics.output: Button darkens and lifts 2px over 180ms on hover; it does not jump.

topics.title: Transform moves without reflow
topics.body: translate, rotate, scale aur skew element ko paint stage par badalte hain, isliye aas-paas ka layout nahi hilta. Multiple functions ek hi transform me likho.

  .panel.open { display: block; opacity: 1; }
</style>
debug.fix:

  .panel { opacity: 0; visibility: hidden; transition: opacity 200ms ease, visibility 200ms; }
  .panel.open { opacity: 1; visibility: visible; }
</style>
debug.error: display is not interpolable: the element jumps from no box to a box, so there are no intermediate frames to transition.

interviewBank.q: Which properties are cheap to animate?
interviewBank.answer: transform and opacity, because they can be handled on the compositor without layout or paint. Animating width, top or box-shadow forces more work each frame.

interviewBank.q: What does transform do to layout?
interviewBank.answer: Nothing. It changes the visual rendering after layout, so neighbours do not move and the original space is preserved.

defenseBank.q: A learner animates width for a progress bar.
defenseBank.answer: Animating width triggers layout on every frame. A transform scaleX on an inner bar gives the same visual with far less work.
steps: Show the layout cost in DevTools.

defenseBank.answer: Large movement and parallax can cause nausea and vestibular symptoms. A prefers-reduced-motion query should remove or shorten non-essential motion.

mcqBank.q: Which property defines how long a transition takes?
mcqBank.why: Duration is the time the transition runs.
translate shifts position without affecting layout.

topics.title: Keyframes and the animation shorthand
topics.body: @keyframes named steps define karta hai; animation property name, duration, easing, delay, iteration aur direction leti hai. Shorthand order careful rakho.

topics.output: A green dot that gently shrinks and fades to half opacity, then returns, forever.

topics.title: Reduced motion and performance
topics.body: prefers-reduced-motion query essential motion ko kam ya band karta hai. Sirf transform aur opacity animate karo taaki layout aur paint ka kaam kam ho.

debug.title: A keyframes name that never matches
debug.broken:
<style>
  @keyframes fadeUp { from { opacity: 0; } to { opacity: 1; } }
  .card { animation: fade-up 400ms ease both; }
</style>
debug.fix:
<style>
  @keyframes fade-up { from { opacity: 0; } to { opacity: 1; } }
  .card { animation: fade-up 400ms ease both; }
</style>
debug.error: Name mismatch: keyframe names are case-sensitive and must match exactly, so no animation is attached.

debug.title: An animation that snaps back at the end
debug.broken:
<style>
  @keyframes lift { to { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(-8px); } }
  .toast { animation: lift 300ms ease; }
</style>
debug.fix:
<style>
  @keyframes lift { to { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(-8px); } }
  .toast { animation: lift 300ms ease forwards; }
</style>
debug.error: No fill mode: after the animation ends the element returns to its base style, so the toast flashes back into view.
debug.fixedOutput: Toast stays faded and lifted after the animation.

tasks.expected: A green dot pulsing gently; it becomes a static dot with reduced motion.

interviewBank.q: Animation or transition — which do you use?
interviewBank.answer: A transition interpolates between two states and needs a state change. An animation runs named keyframes with its own timing and can loop, so multi-step or repeating motion uses @keyframes.
They keep the compositor and sometimes the main thread busy, drain battery, and distract or nauseate users. Use them for short, meaningful states and respect reduced motion.

defenseBank.q: A learner copies a spinner with 20 keyframe steps.
defenseBank.answer: A few keyframes with transform are enough and cheaper. More steps only make sense for a specific visual path.

defenseBank.q: Why guard an animation with reduced motion?
defenseBank.answer: The user has told the system that motion makes them unwell. Ignoring it is an accessibility failure, not a style preference.

interviewBank.q: How are custom properties different from Sass variables?
interviewBank.answer: They are live CSS values that participate in the cascade and can be changed per element, per media query or at runtime. Sass variables are resolved at build time.

interviewBank.q: Why is var() invalid sometimes even with a fallback?
interviewBank.answer: The fallback is used only when the property is missing or invalid at computed-value time. If the fallback itself is invalid, the declaration is still dropped.

defenseBank.q: A learner hardcodes the same blue in twelve files.
defenseBank.answer: One token makes a rebrand a single edit and keeps light and dark themes consistent. Repeated literals drift.

defenseBank.q: Why not put every value in a variable?
defenseBank.answer: Tokens should name decisions, not every number. A variable per declaration adds indirection without reuse and makes the stylesheet harder to read.

mcqBank.q: Which function reads a custom property?
mcqBank.why: var() substitutes a custom property value.

mcqBank.q: Where are global tokens usually declared?
mcqBank.why: :root matches the document element and is the usual token scope.

title: Advanced CSS and Modern Features
goal: Understand the cascade, layers and specificity, and use modern layout and effects with progressive enhancement.

topics.title: Cascade, specificity and layers
topics.body: Cascade importance, origin, layer, specificity aur source order se resolve hota hai. @layer se aap poori stylesheet ki priority explicitly set kar sakte ho.
topics.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <title>Layers</title>
  <style>
    @layer base, components;
    @layer components { .btn { background: #2563eb; color: #fff; padding: 10px 16px; } }
    @layer base { .btn { background: #e2e8f0; color: #0f172a; } }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <button class="btn" type="button">Layered</button>
</body>
</html>
topics.output: Blue button: components is declared after base in the layer order, so its rule wins despite both matching equally.

topics.title: Feature queries, container queries and nesting
topics.body: @supports ek feature ke support par styles lagata hai, @container parent ki width par, aur nesting selectors ko ek doosre ke andar likhne deta hai.

<style>
  @layer components, base;
  @layer base { .btn { background: #e2e8f0; } }
  @layer components { .btn { background: #2563eb; } }
</style>
debug.fix:
<style>
  @layer base, components;
  @layer base { .btn { background: #e2e8f0; } }
  @layer components { .btn { background: #2563eb; } }
</style>
debug.error: Layer order reversed: the first declared layer has the lowest priority, so base overrides components no matter the source order.

debug.title: A fixed height that clips text
debug.broken: A long description that needs more room than the fixed height allows.
debug.fix: A long description that grows the card instead of being clipped.
debug.error: Fixed height: the box cannot grow with its content, so the text is cut off. min-height keeps the intended minimum and lets content expand.

interviewBank.q: How do cascade layers change specificity?
interviewBank.answer: They do not. Layers are compared before specificity: a rule in a higher-priority layer beats a more specific rule in a lower one. Specificity only decides inside the same layer.
When a layout or effect has a genuine fallback, such as grid instead of floats or backdrop-filter instead of a solid surface. It should guard the enhancement, not the base experience.

defenseBank.q: A learner adds !important instead of fixing layers.
defenseBank.answer: Important reverses the layer order and makes future overrides harder. Defining layer order explicitly solves the conflict at the source.
It needs support and can be expensive, especially with large blurred areas. A solid or semi-transparent fallback keeps the UI legible where it is unavailable.

topics.title: Selects, checkboxes and validation
topics.body: Select aur checkbox native behaviour retain karo; appearance:none sirf tab use karo jab custom indicator ho. :invalid aur :user-invalid se validation dikhao, red text ke bharose nahi.
topics.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <title>Validation</title>
  <style>
    input:user-invalid { border-color: #dc2626; background: #fef2f2; }
    input:user-valid { border-color: #16a34a; }
    .check { display: flex; gap: 8px; align-items: center; }
    .check input { width: 18px; height: 18px; accent-color: #2563eb; }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <input type="email" required aria-label="Email">
  <label class="check"><input type="checkbox"> Remember me</label>
</body>
</html>
topics.output: Email field turns red only after invalid input is committed and green when valid; the checkbox uses the blue accent colour.

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <title>Register</title>
  <style>
    form { display: grid; gap: 14px; max-width: 340px; }
    label { font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; }

interviewBank.q: Why keep native form controls when custom styling exists?
interviewBank.answer: Native controls bring keyboard behaviour, platform conventions and assistive-technology support. Replacing them means rebuilding all of that, usually incompletely.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between :invalid and :user-invalid?
interviewBank.answer: :invalid matches immediately, including an empty required field on first render. :user-invalid waits until the user has interacted and the value is still invalid, which avoids a form that is red before typing.

defenseBank.q: A designer wants placeholders instead of labels.
defenseBank.answer: A placeholder disappears on typing and is not a reliable label. Keep a persistent visible label and use the placeholder only for an example.

defenseBank.q: Why not style a div as a checkbox?
defenseBank.answer: It loses keyboard toggling, focus and the checked state exposed to assistive technology. A native input with accent-color is both accessible and styleable enough.

mcqBank.q: Which property tints a native checkbox?
mcqBank.why: accent-color sets the native control accent.

mcqBank.q: Which attribute ties a label to an input?
mcqBank.why: for must match the input id.

interviewBank.answer: It makes class names predictable and collision-resistant by encoding block, element and modifier, so a team can read markup and know which stylesheet owns it.
A reset removes defaults so every element starts from zero; normalize preserves useful defaults while fixing browser differences. Most modern projects use a small targeted reset plus tokens.

defenseBank.q: A learner wants a utility class for every property.
defenseBank.answer: Utilities explode in number and hide intent in markup. Component classes keep the design decisions in CSS; utilities are best for spacing and layout exceptions.
A global list-style:none removes meaning from content lists. Resets should target the components that need them, not every element of a type.

<!DOCTYPE html>

    .cta { background: #1d4ed8; color: #fff; padding: 12px 18px; border: 0; border-radius: 8px; transition: transform 160ms ease; }
    .cta:hover { transform: translateY(-1px); }
    .cta:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #93c5fd; outline-offset: 2px; }
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .cta { transition: none; } }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <button class="cta" type="button">Get started</button>
</body>
</html>
tasks.expected: High-contrast blue button, visible keyboard ring, a 1px lift on hover and no motion when reduced motion is requested.

interviewBank.q: How do you debug “my CSS is not applying”?
interviewBank.answer: Check the network entry and the selector match first, then the Styles panel for a winning rule, then specificity and source order. I change one variable at a time.

interviewBank.q: What causes layout thrash and how do you avoid it?
interviewBank.answer: Reading layout properties and then writing styles repeatedly forces synchronous reflow. Batch reads, batch writes, and animate transform and opacity instead of geometry.

defenseBank.q: A learner adds more CSS to fight a bug.
defenseBank.answer: Adding rules increases the chance of another conflict. I find which rule is winning and fix that rule instead of layering another one on top.

defenseBank.q: Why include accessibility in a debugging checklist?
defenseBank.answer: Contrast, focus and reduced motion break for real users and are cheap to catch before release. They are functional requirements, not polish.

mcqBank.q: Which DevTools panel shows the final value of a property?
mcqBank.why: The Computed panel shows resolved values after the cascade.

mcqBank.q: Which animation is cheapest for the browser?
mcqBank.why: transform can run on the compositor without layout.

mini.title: Bug hunt
mini.brief: Take a page with three layout bugs and document each cause before fixing it.

lab.brief: Run a CSS release checklist over a page: contrast, focus, reduced motion, unused rules and layout at three widths.
